A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same function-induction study. Their complete main texts and appendices provide readable, matchable figures, tables, equations, and experimental descriptions despite substantial renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model evaluations, circuit-discovery and ablation experiments, causal-intervention heatmaps, and task-generalization analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds Llama-2 circuit discovery, previous-token-head ablations, and causal analyses of additional head groups.

M1.justification: The core path-patching procedure and pretrained models remain unchanged. Appendix F.3 introduces a limited adaptation of the causal probe for previous-token heads: averaging outputs across demonstration-answer positions and injecting them at an earlier answer token in the naive prompt, rather than the final '=' used for FI-head probing.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same arithmetic ranges and offsets, six MMLU subjects, Caesar-cipher variants, and addition bases. The new analyses use retained tasks; extending circuit analysis to Llama-2 changes model coverage within the evaluation settings, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds an explicit structural comparison between its Llama-2 FI heads and ten FV heads selected from Todd et al. (2024), comparing membership and layer locations in Section 4 and Appendix D.2.4. This uses previously reported head identities, not a newly run task-performance baseline. Existing benchmark comparators and ablation-control methods are retained.

E3.justification: New experiments include 4-shot Llama-2 circuit discovery on numbers in [0,9], 16-shot previous-token-head ablations with an eight-random-head control, and causal probing using outputs extracted from 100 4-shot examples. Previously reported circuit-discovery, benchmark, and task-generalization settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices F.2–F.3 substantially extend validation beyond FI heads: new interventions examine consolidation-head outputs, previous-token-head necessity, and previous-token-head causal effects. Appendix D.2.4 also adds cross-model circuit analysis and FI/FV-head comparison. The faithfulness, completeness, and minimality analyses in Appendix E already appeared in v1 Section 4.

E5.justification: Existing error-bar displays are retained without new seed counts, repeated-run disclosures, confidence intervals, or statistical-testing procedures. The new previous-token ablation table reports point accuracies without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantive mechanistic results. Table 5 reports that ablating previous-token heads reduces off-by-one accuracy from 86% to 4% and off-by-two accuracy from 46% to 1%. Figures 26–27 add opposing consolidation-head effects and previous-token-head effects; Figure 16 adds Llama-2 findings. Existing benchmark results, Table 3, and 78.4% circuit faithfulness are retained. Figure 5's rescaling does not establish changed results.

T1.justification: The logit-difference definitions, normalization equations, circuit-evaluation criteria, and illustrative base-8 algorithm remain equivalent. Moving the circuit criteria into Appendix E and adding mechanistic hypotheses introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: Both abstracts retain the same three contributions: function-level induction, distributed contributions from multiple heads, and reuse across task pairs. The introduction and conclusion emphasize latent multi-step reasoning more explicitly, but the contribution scope is unchanged. Llama-2 supplies additional support for the retained universality claim.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands mechanistic interpretation: consolidation heads may weigh competing answers, grouped-query attention may encourage opposing head effects, and late FI heads may specialize in multi-step tasks. It attributes unexpected previous-token effects partly to task shift and token averaging. Existing completeness and task-scope limitations remain, while v1's broader-impact discussion of misinformation and sycophancy is removed.

D1.justification: v2 supplies Llama-2 head lists and selection details, specifies previous-token activation averaging and injection positions, and explicitly states Gemma-2's layer/head counts. These improve procedural documentation. The software libraries, A6000 hardware, approximate path-patching runtime, model identifiers, and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work inventory is retained, but v2 sharpens positioning relative to Todd et al. through the disjoint FI/FV-head comparison and a late-layer specialization hypothesis. It also connects opposing head effects to previously cited interpretability challenges. Citation-format changes alone are not counted here.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main-section sequence remain intact. Reorganization focuses on Section 4: it is renamed and refocused, formal circuit evaluation moves to Appendix E, and circuit analyses are regrouped in Appendix F. Limitations move to Appendix A. Local wording and citation-style edits accompany these changes; some obsolete Figure 4 panel references remain.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template and substantially reorganizes central displays. The original three-panel Figure 4 becomes a standalone ablation figure plus Appendix Figure 21; rescaled panels formerly in Appendix Figure 20 are incorporated into Figure 5. It also adds Llama-2 and head-effect figures and Table 5. Most remaining plot contents are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix F partly addresses v1's stated need to investigate previous-token and consolidation heads, adding direct ablation evidence and causal-effect maps. Llama-2 replication further strengthens empirical support. These are useful gains, but circuit faithfulness remains 78.4%, completeness remains partial, and several new explanations remain hypotheses. Minor cross-reference errors accompany the reorganization. Overall, v2 provides better-supported interpretation without resolving the study's central remaining limitations.
